title: Reunion
essence: Decades later, the poet hosts his brothers and friends in the white temple he built in 11: hugs with no reason, laughter, football on a wall screen, an old snapshot restaged. Underneath the noise one quantity only grows, the distance between two brothers, from a hug to talking distance to the width of a memory, while a yard of burning hourglasses goes out one by one until a single one is left, and its last ember drifts out over the sea through the gap the wind opened.
palette_notes: Bone-white plaster #ece6da and warm sandstone #c99765 (the poem's own colour in film/poems.json) come from the colonnaded pavilion in 08fe12af_0; pool turquoise #2fa3a8 is the same still's water; #8a6a4a is the dark wood of the hourglass ends and the low benches. Dusk indigo #3a3f63 and near-black #14121c are the night mirror corridor in 58cbb4ca_0, used for the ELDERS movement when the polarity turns over; the violet star-fleck #7b6fd6 is the starlit black pool of f05c1fa5_1 (the afterlives). The one hot accent is ember orange #e0632a: hourglass flames and the last drifting ember, nothing else in the poem is allowed to be that colour.

full_text.line: Decades later, there was less time for words and more space for laughter, hugs with no reason,
loud voices so our hearts can be overheard. My mind drifts into the darkness of our afterlives,
and those rooms are empty. We are all here, each holding hourglasses of burning sands
and known journeys, and grateful to every living tree in the forest for the shared airs
and the shared memories. This is brotherhood. Smiles with no reason,
narrow differences so our hearts can be overheard. Decades later, we can place our ears upon the next
brother's soul and follow paths of hilltops and canyons, of blinding lights and infinite nights,
all too familiar and create the type of space for laughter
and football and recollections that bring us home every time.

characters.design_notes: Not puppets: negative cut-outs. Build as a black drop with elder silhouettes cut through it, backlit pale; they do not breathe while the brothers do, which is the whole difference between a living man and a memory.

insights: The poem is about distance that grows while love does not shrink: keep the brothers' gap a single number that only widens (hug ~15, talking 28-52, memory 54-70, terrace wider) and never animate them walking toward each other.
Words shrink, they never erode: the printed word cards go smaller movement to movement; a half-dissolved glyph is noise.

ELDERS is the one polarity flip in the film: paper becomes ink and the elders are holes in it; build them as negative cut-outs in a drop, not as puppets, and let the drop drain rather than the elders walk off.

Twelve hourglasses on a grid, nudged clear of the brothers' heads (flames off a crown read as a candelabra), going out in a coprime order; the count of the ones still lit IS the question 'is this a one-time occasion?'.
Orange is reserved for fire; the temple is bone, sandstone and turquoise by day and indigo/violet by night.
Transcript corrections from the treatment: 'our glasses' is 'hourglasses'; 'shared years' is 'shared airs' in the treatment, check against the voice before setting type.

Atlas: the foundry's ink hourglass drawing (foundry/12-03) is the right graphic language for the whole hourglass yard: flat black wood ends, dotted sand, notched flame cards. Do not render glass realistically.
Atlas: the reunion is shot down the nave in symmetry and doubled in a black floor; one gloss reflection pass on the floor card does more for 'the white temple' than any wall detail.
Atlas: keep the chapel's flood line visible under the white plates; it is what makes this the same building as 03 and 11.
Atlas: the archive's group portraits (archive/2696, 6946) fix the snapshot composition: frontal rows, seated in front, everyone looking at camera; the restaging must match it card for card.
future: temple_hall and the terrace become the harbor edge of 13 and the 'temple' that turns to haze in 14.
The burning hourglass is the ninth and last motif card in 14's reel.
The family kit (brother, friends, elders) is reused for 13's couples and elders and 14's everyday people.
Sunglasses come off on the terrace; in 13 taking them off becomes the refocus.

atlas.district_language: The White Temple is the Shore realm's one interior: storm and ruin outside, a hall full of people inside, decades later. Paint it as the city's purest ceramic: bone-white plates on the chapel's old dark stone, every plate joint drawn with a thin cyan seam (the brightest seam in the city; a Glazier drew it), and the chapel's flood line kept as a faint grey-blue tide mark at 4/10 of wall height under the vault, never painted over. Light is not lamps but the white ceramic itself lit by the sky: code one warm bounce gradient on the white wall cards that cools from 17:30 gold to 19:45 blue, and let the only point lights be the hourglass flames, the wall screen, and at the end a single porch bulb. Floors are mirror pools: a black gloss card under each set that doubles whatever stands on it (code a flipped, darkened, 2px-rippled copy). The hall is wide and symmetrical, shot down the nave; outside, the camera goes low to the water. Never show the city's neon here, never a second light colour besides warm amber and seam cyan, and never a clean wall at the flood line.

staging.name: Welcome home in the hall
staging.shot: Locked wide from high up the nave (the 'rafters' view), symmetrical: back plane is the end wall with one arched window, mid planes are three pairs of niche-pier cards stepping toward camera, floor is the black gloss card doubling everyone. Friends enter from the colonnade at frame right in a staggered line; the circle forms centre floor. Cut to a handheld-feel medium (coded 1-2px drift) inside the circle as two pairs hug and rock.

staging.name: Loud voices, overheard hearts
staging.shot: Chest-height mediums, three or four quick cuts on laughter: background is the white niche wall blurred (a softened copy of the wall card), foreground shoulders cross frame out of focus. On each shout a warm ring pulses from the speaker's chest (heard_rings fx). Crowd motion as smeared duplicate silhouettes.

staging.name: The empty rooms of the afterlife
staging.shot: Tilt up the white pier card into the dark of the vault (gradient to black), then a hard cut to a static wide of a side room: rows of empty folding chairs on bare boards under one sagging wire of bulbs, a single chair turned away at the foot of a lit stair. Nothing moves except dust motes and one bulb's flicker.

staging.name: Hourglasses and the group photo
staging.shot: Locked frontal tableau composed exactly like the old snapshot: two rows, the seated row on the low dark benches, the standing row behind, each figure holding a burning hand hourglass at waist. The snapshot card is held up in the foreground lower left, then lowered as the live group matches it. Macro insert: dotted sand falling through the neck, flame on the rim. Phone flash (camera_flash) whites out one frame.

staging.name: Trees at the forest edge
staging.shot: Low angle up into a canopy card (dark green cut leaves, string of picnic bulbs looping between trunks); slow lateral pan along three trunk cards in the mid layer as friends lay palms on the bark. Faint memory images projected on a fog card behind (tracing-paper layer with a looping old-film texture).

staging.name: Brotherhood chain
staging.shot: Profile track left to right down a chain of men on a sandy path, wrists interlocked, heads leaning together; the camera stops on the poet with his ear to BROTHER_1's chest. Insert: interlocked wrists. The sea is a flat band behind, the sky going blue.

staging.name: Football in the meadow, then home
staging.shot: Golden-hour wide: meadow as three grass strip cards, the hill line behind, the football card arcing through frame on a coded parabola with a 4-frame spin cycle. Polaroids flutter down as paper cards. Final: from behind the group, their backs a single silhouette row, climbing porch steps toward the temple door as a bulb switches on; its reflection lands in the pool of stars.

heroes.name: The Temple's Pools
heroes.in_poem: The hall's floor and the terrace are both pools: every hug in 12.0 is doubled in the black floor, and the last ember (and then the porch bulb) is reflected in the pool of stars. The portico pool gives the 11 to 12 cut: same frame, filled with people.
heroes.build_as_cards: Three gloss-black floor cards (hall floor, portico pool, star pool) with a coded reflection pass: flipped copy of the layers above, 60% darkness, 2px horizontal ripple that settles. The portico pool is a facade card of seven white columns with two tree cards either side; the star pool has a mitred stone rim card in the foreground and a star field painted on the water card that stays put while the sky drifts. Tambourine fragments from 03 are set into the pool rim as small white plates.

transitions.how: A walk: the poet leaves the porch in daylight the next day and the camera begins a long lateral along the water past the drowned atrium (a glowing floor card under still water, trees in planters) to the café. Shared card: the portico pool's reflection is wiped right-to-left into the atrium's glowing floor.
Ellipsis on a locked frame: the empty mirror hall plate from 11 is held, then the same plate cuts to filled with people, decades later; nothing in the architecture moves.
